name: Gather Grove Booking
author: gturtle108

sections.description:
Gather Grove Booking runs the schedule for people who teach — yoga and fitness studios, dance and martial arts schools, music teachers, pottery and craft studios, wellness practitioners, and community programs. Put your booking pages on any theme or page builder — or design them visually with Elementor — take drop-in and appointment bookings, and accept card payments with Stripe.

The free version is fully functional for running a real studio:

  • Classes & sessions — recurring schedules, capacity limits, multiple locations and rooms.
  • Online booking — a booking form and schedule your clients use to reserve a spot, as shortcodes for any page builder or as Elementor widgets.
  • Appointments — bookable service slots with availability windows and optional deposits.
  • Waivers & liability forms — collect a real signature as part of booking, then see your whole roster at a glance: who has signed the current version, who signed an older one, whose signature has expired, and who has never signed at all. Send reminders by hand, record a paper signature, or export the lot to CSV.
  • Passwordless sign-in — students can sign in with a link emailed to them instead of a password, so nobody is locked out of a booking by a password they never set. Optional, and you choose whether your site offers passwords, magic links, or both.
  • Waitlists — clients can join a waitlist when a class is full, and open spots are automatically offered to the next person in line.
  • Flexible schedules — a class can meet on multiple recurring schedule blocks (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri at different times).
  • Bulk attendance marking — mark a whole roster present in one action.
  • Payments — accept cards through Stripe for drop-in bookings.
  • Client accounts — a self-service dashboard for bookings and profile.
  • Attendance — front-desk and instructor check-in.
  • Instructors & locations — profiles, assignments, and per-location schedules.

Who it’s for

  • Yoga, pilates and fitness studios — recurring drop-in classes, capacity limits, waitlists, and a signed waiver on file before anyone steps on a mat.
  • Dance and martial arts schools — several weekly schedule blocks on one class, per-location rooms, and front-desk check-in.
  • Music teachers and schools — appointment-style lessons with availability windows and optional deposits, alongside recurring group classes.
  • Pottery, craft and maker studios — small capacities, multiple rooms, and a roster you can mark present in one action.
  • Wellness practitioners — one-to-one appointments shown in the visitor’s own timezone, with a self-service client dashboard.
  • Breathwork, meditation and sound-healing facilitators — circles, workshops and sound baths with capacity limits, a waitlist when they fill, and a waiver signed before anyone arrives.
  • Coaches, mentors and private sessions — bookable one-to-one slots with availability windows and optional deposits, so clients pick a time without the back-and-forth.
  • Online facilitators — virtual classes and appointments, with the Zoom meeting created for you and the join link in every confirmation and reminder.
  • Community programs and co-ops — free and comp bookings with no payment gateway required, and waiver compliance across a whole roster.

Any theme, any builder

The client-facing pages (schedule, booking form, appointment booking, member account, login) come as shortcodes for any theme or page builder — WPBakery, Gutenberg, Divi, a classic theme — and as Elementor widgets if you design with Elementor (3.5 or newer). Elementor Pro is optional: it adds dynamic tags and Theme Builder templates.

In your language

Booking ships with an Italian translation, and prices and dates follow your site language: an Italian site shows “22,00 €” and “martedì 20 ottobre”, an American one “$22.00” and “Tuesday, October 20”. Dates and times use your WordPress date and time format unless you set Booking’s own, and the calendar starts the week on your “Week Starts On” day.

Part of the Gather Grove suite

Gather Grove Booking works entirely on its own. It is also one part of Gather Grove, a family of plugins for running and growing a creative business on your own WordPress site. The plugins share one admin, one list of people, and one look, so a studio can add what it needs as it grows:

  • Gather Grove Pulse — email broadcasts, automated sequences and a contact list that knows who booked, joined or enrolled.
  • Gather Grove Communities — private member spaces with rooms, an activity feed and direct messages.
  • Gather Grove Courses — self-paced and cohort-based online courses.
  • Gather Grove Forms — applications, intake forms and RSVPs that feed the rest of the suite.
  • Gather Grove Companion — an AI assistant for your admin, and a chat helper for your visitors.
  • Gather Grove Notion Sync — free; sends bookings and form entries to your Notion workspace.

Together they serve creators, mentors, facilitators and anyone running a private community or an online program, as well as studios. Learn more at gathergrove.io.

Free and Professional

Everything listed above is free, and stays free. The free plugin has no locked features, never expires, and is not a trial.

Gather Grove Booking Professional is a separate plugin, available from gathergrove.io, for studios that sell more than drop-ins. It adds:

  • Memberships and class packs
  • Gift cards
  • Family and household accounts
  • Multi-instructor scheduling
  • Enrollment-style courses
  • Custom email branding
  • Advanced reporting drill-downs

Compare every feature, line by line, at gathergrove.io/docs/pricing.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services.

Stripe — used to process card payments after you connect a Stripe account and a client pays for a booking or appointment. The booking and payment details required to create the charge (amount, currency, and related metadata) are sent to Stripe at payment time. Stripe.js is loaded from Stripe’s servers on pages that display a payment form, as required for PCI compliance.
Terms of service: https://stripe.com/legal — Privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Google Maps — used by the optional Location “Map Embed” and “Directions Link” Elementor dynamic tags. If you place the Map Embed tag on a page, the visitor’s browser loads an embedded map from google.com for the location’s address (Google receives the visitor’s IP address and the studio address, as with any embedded map). The Directions Link tag only builds a link to google.com/maps containing the studio address; nothing is sent unless the visitor clicks it. No data is sent from your server, and neither tag is active unless you add it to a page.
Terms of service: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Zoom — used to automatically create, update, and delete Zoom meetings for virtual class and appointment sessions, only after you connect your own Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app under Settings → Integrations. When a virtual booking is confirmed (and on reschedule or cancellation), your server sends the session’s topic, start time, duration, timezone, and the host’s email address to api.zoom.us / zoom.us using your own credentials. Nothing is sent unless you enable the integration, and visitors’ browsers never contact Zoom through this plugin.
Terms of service: https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://explore.zoom.us/en/privacy/

Postmark — used to send your site’s email through your own Postmark account, only after you connect one under Gather Grove → Settings → Email delivery. When connected, your server sends Postmark your key, your sending domain (to register it and check its DNS records), and each email it is asked to send: sender, recipients, subject, body and any attachments. If you also switch on “Send all your site’s email through Postmark”, every email your site sends goes this way. Postmark then posts delivery, bounce, open, click, spam-complaint and unsubscribe reports back to a secret address on your site. Nothing is sent unless you connect an account.
Terms of service: https://postmarkapp.com/terms-of-service — Privacy policy: https://postmarkapp.com/privacy-policy

Web push services (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft) — when a member turns on phone notifications, their browser registers with its own push service, and your site sends each notification to that service for delivery. The notification carries a short title and a link. The push service receives it with the member’s browser subscription address, and with your site’s admin email address, which the web push standard requires as a contact for the sending site. Nothing is sent unless a member turns notifications on.
Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy — Mozilla privacy policy: https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/ — Apple privacy policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/ — Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
sections.installation:
1. Optional: install Elementor if you want to design your booking pages visually. Without it, every page is a shortcode.
  2. Upload the gather-grove-booking folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  3. Activate Gather Grove Booking through the Plugins screen.
  4. Go to Gather Grove → Settings to configure your studio, then connect Stripe under the Payments tab.
  5. Use Gather Grove → Getting Started to create your booking and schedule pages.
sections.faq:
Do I need Elementor?

No. Every client page is also a shortcode — see Using Gather Grove without Elementor. Elementor (3.5 or newer) is supported if you prefer to build pages with its editor; if it is older than 3.5 the widgets stay switched off and a notice asks you to update.

Do I need the other Gather Grove plugins?

No. Booking is complete on its own. The other Gather Grove plugins are optional and add email, communities, courses, forms and more when you want them.

Do I need Elementor Pro?

No. Elementor Pro is optional. It adds dynamic tags and automatic Theme Builder starter pages, but every booking feature works without it — and without Elementor at all.

How are payments processed?

Card payments are processed by Stripe. You connect your own Stripe account; Gather Grove never stores card numbers on your site.

Does it work without a payment gateway?

Yes. You can run free classes, complimentary (comp) bookings, and offline/invoice payments without connecting Stripe.

Will my data be deleted if I uninstall?

No. Uninstalling leaves your studio data intact by default so you can reinstall safely. You can opt in to full data deletion under Settings → General → Danger Zone.

Does it change anything about my site’s login or security?

Two small protections are on by default, shared by every Gather Grove plugin. Visitors who are not logged in can no longer read your site’s list of account names (WordPress normally publishes it at /wp-json/wp/v2/users and through ?author= links). And after 10 failed logins from one address in 15 minutes, that address has to wait before trying again, on the WordPress login page and on Gather Grove’s own sign-in form. Logged-in editors are not affected, and sites behind Cloudflare are recognised automatically. If you already use a security plugin, or need the public account list, return false from the gather_grove/security/throttle_logins or gather_grove/security/hide_user_list filter to turn either off.

Can I style the widgets using my real classes in the Elementor editor?

Yes. Gather Grove widgets show a styleable sample by default in the Elementor editor. To style against your actual content, open the widget’s Content tab, find the “Editor Preview” section, and set “Preview in editor” to “Real data” (for the Class Card widget, also pick a specific class). The editor canvas then renders your real class so you can style it without switching to the live page. This is rolling out across the widgets — the Class Card and Sessions List widgets have it today, with more on the way. It only affects the editor; your published page always shows live data.
sections.changelog:
1.269.1

  • Fixed: an ongoing-group membership that charges the first period at sign-up and prorates it now measures the share against the sessions in a whole period. Someone joining with 2 of the month’s 5 sessions left pays 2/5 of the fee, not the whole fee.
  • Fixed: when someone picks a first session after the next due day, they now pay today for the period that session falls in (prorated if the membership prorates) and are next charged when that period ends. Before, nothing was charged today and the full fee was taken on the earlier due day. With SEPA Direct Debit that €0 sign-up never set up the mandate, so the renewal could not be collected and the membership ended.
  • Fixed: a membership paid by SEPA Direct Debit (or another bank debit) whose first payment is nothing today (billing waits for the due day or start date, or credit or a promo covers it) now sets up the bank mandate at checkout, so the first regular payment can be collected. If the account can’t be set up, checkout says so and the membership isn’t started.
  • Changed: the note under “When would you like to start?” now shows what is charged today and until when, for every start, also when the first period is not prorated.

1.269.0

  • Changed (Italian): every package is now a “carnet”, the word Italian studios use, so the screens no longer mix “carnet” and “pacchetto”.
  • Fixed: when we don’t know someone’s name, greetings now read “Hi!” (Italian “Ciao!”) instead of “Hi there” (“Ciao a te”). This covers waivers, receipts, gift cards, space rentals, course claims and instructor messages.
  • Fixed: “Credit” and “Joined” can now be translated differently where they mean different things. In Italian, a booking covered by a session credit shows “Ingresso”, while the money balance stays “Credito”.
  • Fixed: on a studio that charges in euros or pounds, amount labels (“Amount Paid”, “Fixed”, class price limits), minimum-amount messages and editor preview prices showed “$”. They now use the studio’s currency.
  • Fixed: after moving an appointment from the “Manage booking” page, the new date is written in the site’s language rather than the browser’s.

1.268.2

  • Fixed: the “Go to your course” button on the page you reach after confirming a free course claim had no visible label (dark text on a dark button). The same fix covers the “Log in” button on the link-already-used page.
  • Fixed: on iPhone, tapping the promo code box beside a course’s Buy or Enroll button no longer zooms the page in.

1.268.1

  • Fixed: on a site whose brand Primary colour is light, the text on primary buttons (Book, the calendar toolbar, checkout and more) could be nearly invisible. Those labels now switch to dark text when the light one cannot be read. Includes Gather Grove core 0.90.0.

1.268.0

1.267.0

1.266.1

  • Fixed: when the first payment of a membership checkout fails, the membership no longer goes past due. It stays unstarted (no booking access, and the person can check out again); they get an email with a link to try the payment again, and staff are told the signup payment failed and that Stripe won’t retry it. If it isn’t paid within about 23 hours, the checkout is closed and the person is told they weren’t charged.
  • Changed: the Italian translation uses the words Italian studios use: carnet, ingressi (classes left) vs credito (money), cliente, buono regalo, codice sconto, Area riservata, and “tu” throughout.

1.266.0

  • Fixed: studio credit used on a membership’s first payment now covers only what is charged that day; the rest stays in the member’s credit.

1.265.0

1.264.0

  • Added: parents can add their child right in the membership checkout (“+ Add a family member” under “Who is this for?”) and buy the membership for them without leaving the page.

1.263.0

  • Added: importing from a spreadsheet with Gather Grove Migrate (0.4.0-alpha or later) can put clients’ remaining classes onto a pack or membership you already set up in Booking, instead of creating a copy of it.
  • Changed: Migrate’s import wizard starts with your studio’s currency.
  • Changed: more of Booking is translated into Italian (sliding scale, bookings export, seats, the waiver step).

1.262.1

  • Fixed: free build packaging (no user-facing change).

1.262.0

  • Added: a client who already holds a membership can buy the same one for someone in their household with “Buy for a Household Member”.
  • Added: on a members-only class, the booking form greys out anyone in the household who doesn’t hold the membership, with a “Get a membership” link. The same link appears if a booking is refused because a membership is needed.
  • Fixed: “Buy for Someone Else” on a pack or membership you already own opens as a gift again, with the gift box ticked and locked.

1.261.0

  • Added: Bookings can be filtered by class date (from / to, both days included, in your site’s time zone).

  • Added: Export CSV on the Bookings screen downloads every booking that matches your filters, with one row per person attending (each seat of a group booking gets its own row).

  • Fixed: Clients Export CSV downloads a clean spreadsheet again. Before, the file could end up mixed into the admin page instead of downloading.

  • Fixed: a sliding-scale class with no drop-in price showed no price at all on its class page.
  • Changed: the sliding-scale settings moved from Booking Rules to the Pricing section, right under Drop-in Price, and stay there for courses too (where they apply to the Course Price).
  • Fixed: on a free class, the waiver step no longer says “Payment comes after”, and the seats help no longer mentions package credits or refunds that don’t apply.

1.257.1

  • Fixed: a site running Booking alongside other Gather Grove plugins could stop with a “critical error” on every page when Booking carried the newest shared core. Includes Gather Grove core 0.89.0, which prevents it.

1.257.0

1.256.1

  • Fixed: the free version is packaged without the membership-invoice code it doesn’t use. No change to how Booking works.

1.256.0

  • Changed: includes Gather Grove core 0.88.0. Every marketing email carries your studio’s postal address (set it under Settings → Email delivery → Marketing email details), email always goes out from your verified sending address, and Tools → Export / Erase Personal Data now covers all of Gather Grove.
  • Fixed: marketing emails (news and offers, birthday, win-back and the rest) are no longer sent without your studio’s postal address, which the law requires in every marketing email. Until you add it under Settings → Email delivery → Marketing email details, they are held back and the message log says why. Booking confirmations, reminders and receipts are never affected.
  • New: a notice on Booking’s screens tells you when marketing emails are switched on but your postal address is missing, with a link to add it. System Status shows it too.
  • New: WordPress’s Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data tools (Tools menu) now include everything Booking keeps about a client: their profile, bookings and appointments, memberships and packs, payments and invoices, waivers, documents, studio notes and the emails sent to them — including bookings made under an old email address. Erasing keeps your financial records (amounts and dates) but removes the person’s name, contact details, notes and documents, and clears their name and email in Stripe. Booking does not cancel an active membership for you; the erase screen tells you if one is still billing.

1.255.0

  • Changed: includes Gather Grove core 0.86.0. After a site moves to a new address, a “This site moved” checklist shows what was updated and what still needs you, and email delivery reports follow the site. Someone who unsubscribed now confirms by email before they get news and offers again.
  • New: when your site moves to a new address (a new host, or a switch to https or www) and you confirm “This is the live site now”, Booking points your Stripe connection at the new address by itself, so payments, renewals and refunds keep showing up on your site. The connection at the old address is switched off in Stripe (not deleted), and anything else on your Stripe account is left alone. The “This site moved” notice tells you whether it worked, with a link to fix it if not.
  • New: after a move, the same notice reminds you that instructors who added their class calendar to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook need to add it again with their new link (shown on their instructor page).
  • Changed: when someone who unsubscribed turns “email me news” back on in their account, they now get one email asking them to confirm, and news starts only after they click it. Until then their account says “Check your email to confirm” instead of showing them as subscribed.
  • Changed: when someone unsubscribes using a link sent to an email address that also belongs to a member’s account (for example a child booked under a parent’s email), that account is unsubscribed from marketing email too. Confirmations, reminders and receipts still go.

1.254.0

  • Fixed: when someone unsubscribes from a Pulse email, marks one as spam, or turns marketing email back on, their client record in Booking now shows the same choice straight away, and your email-list exports follow it.

  • Fixed: an email address that permanently bounced, or that marked your email as spam, no longer gets Booking’s marketing emails (birthday greeting, win-back and the rest).

  • Fixed: when the phone number is required, its label no longer says “(optional)” in Italian.
  • Fixed: the class card list shows three cards on a desktop, two on a tablet and one on a phone; the package shop fits three packages on a laptop-width row.
  • Fixed: a class pack past its expiry date shows under “Expired packages” in the member’s account instead of as active.
  • Fixed: Front Desk and the instructor dashboard list everyone in a past class, with their check-in, after bookings are marked attended.
  • Changed: clearer wording — “Upcoming classes”, “All classes”, “All instructors”, “Show all 9 upcoming classes”, “1 / 16 booked” and “7 / 16 booked” in Italian, and the drop-in payment choice now reads “Pay for this class”.
  • Fixed: Front Desk’s date controls fit on a phone, it loads the week once when it opens, and “Last 90 days” on the client card no longer lists future purchases.

1.253.0

  • New: Booking works without Elementor — every client page is also a shortcode, for WPBakery, Gutenberg, Divi and classic themes. Elementor is now optional, and Create studio pages builds ordinary shortcode pages when it is not active.
  • New: Italian translation.
  • New: prices and dates follow your site language. An Italian site now shows “22,00 €” and “martedì 20 ottobre”; English sites look exactly as before.
  • Changed: Booking’s date and time format follow your WordPress date and time format unless you set Booking’s own under Settings → General.
  • Fixed: the schedule calendar and Front Desk calendar show your site language and start the week on your “Week Starts On” day.
  • Fixed: Booking’s default words (instructor, class, studio) and the default email templates now appear in your site language. Your own wording is never changed.

1.252.0

  • New: before you delete a client, Booking tells you what deleting will end, such as a membership that is still charging or studio credit on their record. WordPress’s own delete screen shows the same list.
  • Fixed: a deleted client’s choice not to get marketing email or texts now stays on their client record.
  • Fixed: when someone signs up with the email of a client you deleted, they get a new client record. Before, they silently took over the old one, with its notes, credit and household.

1.251.0

  • Fixed: a gift card refunded in Stripe now loses its value. A full refund voids an unredeemed card and a partial refund lowers its balance. If the card was already added to someone’s studio credit, Booking takes back the credit they still have, never below zero, and tells you if they had already spent some of it.
  • Fixed: Void & refund on a gift card now takes the refund off your revenue reports, once. A lost chargeback on a gift card voids it the same way.

1.250.0

  • New: a chargeback now comes off your revenue when Stripe takes the money, with Stripe’s dispute fee as its own line, so Reports match your Stripe payout. If you win, the money comes back on its own line.
  • New: if you lose a chargeback for a class pack, the pack ends as it would after a full refund, and a drop-in booking shows as refunded. The money is never taken off twice.

short_description: For yoga studios, teachers and community programs — class booking, waivers, appointments, waitlists and Stripe payments. Any theme or page builder.
description:
Gather Grove Booking runs the schedule for people who teach — yoga and fitness studios, dance and martial arts schools, music teachers, pottery and craft studios, wellness practitioners, and community programs. Put your booking pages on any theme or page builder — or design them visually with Elementor — take drop-in and appointment bookings, and accept card payments with Stripe.

The free version is fully functional for running a real studio:

  • Classes & sessions — recurring schedules, capacity limits, multiple locations and rooms.
  • Online booking — a booking form and schedule your clients use to reserve a spot, as shortcodes for any page builder or as Elementor widgets.
  • Appointments — bookable service slots with availability windows and optional deposits.
  • Waivers & liability forms — collect a real signature as part of booking, then see your whole roster at a glance: who has signed the current version, who signed an older one, whose signature has expired, and who has never signed at all. Send reminders by hand, record a paper signature, or export the lot to CSV.
  • Passwordless sign-in — students can sign in with a link emailed to them instead of a password, so nobody is locked out of a booking by a password they never set. Optional, and you choose whether your site offers passwords, magic links, or both.
  • Waitlists — clients can join a waitlist when a class is full, and open spots are automatically offered to the next person in line.
  • Flexible schedules — a class can meet on multiple recurring schedule blocks (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri at different times).
  • Bulk attendance marking — mark a whole roster present in one action.
  • Payments — accept cards through Stripe for drop-in bookings.
  • Client accounts — a self-service dashboard for bookings and profile.
  • Attendance — front-desk and instructor check-in.
  • Instructors & locations — profiles, assignments, and per-location schedules.

Who it’s for

  • Yoga, pilates and fitness studios — recurring drop-in classes, capacity limits, waitlists, and a signed waiver on file before anyone steps on a mat.
  • Dance and martial arts schools — several weekly schedule blocks on one class, per-location rooms, and front-desk check-in.
  • Music teachers and schools — appointment-style lessons with availability windows and optional deposits, alongside recurring group classes.
  • Pottery, craft and maker studios — small capacities, multiple rooms, and a roster you can mark present in one action.
  • Wellness practitioners — one-to-one appointments shown in the visitor’s own timezone, with a self-service client dashboard.
  • Breathwork, meditation and sound-healing facilitators — circles, workshops and sound baths with capacity limits, a waitlist when they fill, and a waiver signed before anyone arrives.
  • Coaches, mentors and private sessions — bookable one-to-one slots with availability windows and optional deposits, so clients pick a time without the back-and-forth.
  • Online facilitators — virtual classes and appointments, with the Zoom meeting created for you and the join link in every confirmation and reminder.
  • Community programs and co-ops — free and comp bookings with no payment gateway required, and waiver compliance across a whole roster.

Any theme, any builder

The client-facing pages (schedule, booking form, appointment booking, member account, login) come as shortcodes for any theme or page builder — WPBakery, Gutenberg, Divi, a classic theme — and as Elementor widgets if you design with Elementor (3.5 or newer). Elementor Pro is optional: it adds dynamic tags and Theme Builder templates.

In your language

Booking ships with an Italian translation, and prices and dates follow your site language: an Italian site shows “22,00 €” and “martedì 20 ottobre”, an American one “$22.00” and “Tuesday, October 20”. Dates and times use your WordPress date and time format unless you set Booking’s own, and the calendar starts the week on your “Week Starts On” day.

Part of the Gather Grove suite

Gather Grove Booking works entirely on its own. It is also one part of Gather Grove, a family of plugins for running and growing a creative business on your own WordPress site. The plugins share one admin, one list of people, and one look, so a studio can add what it needs as it grows:

  • Gather Grove Pulse — email broadcasts, automated sequences and a contact list that knows who booked, joined or enrolled.
  • Gather Grove Communities — private member spaces with rooms, an activity feed and direct messages.
  • Gather Grove Courses — self-paced and cohort-based online courses.
  • Gather Grove Forms — applications, intake forms and RSVPs that feed the rest of the suite.
  • Gather Grove Companion — an AI assistant for your admin, and a chat helper for your visitors.
  • Gather Grove Notion Sync — free; sends bookings and form entries to your Notion workspace.

Together they serve creators, mentors, facilitators and anyone running a private community or an online program, as well as studios. Learn more at gathergrove.io.

Free and Professional

Everything listed above is free, and stays free. The free plugin has no locked features, never expires, and is not a trial.

Gather Grove Booking Professional is a separate plugin, available from gathergrove.io, for studios that sell more than drop-ins. It adds:

  • Memberships and class packs
  • Gift cards
  • Family and household accounts
  • Multi-instructor scheduling
  • Enrollment-style courses
  • Custom email branding
  • Advanced reporting drill-downs

Compare every feature, line by line, at gathergrove.io/docs/pricing.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services.

Stripe — used to process card payments after you connect a Stripe account and a client pays for a booking or appointment. The booking and payment details required to create the charge (amount, currency, and related metadata) are sent to Stripe at payment time. Stripe.js is loaded from Stripe’s servers on pages that display a payment form, as required for PCI compliance.
Terms of service: https://stripe.com/legal — Privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Google Maps — used by the optional Location “Map Embed” and “Directions Link” Elementor dynamic tags. If you place the Map Embed tag on a page, the visitor’s browser loads an embedded map from google.com for the location’s address (Google receives the visitor’s IP address and the studio address, as with any embedded map). The Directions Link tag only builds a link to google.com/maps containing the studio address; nothing is sent unless the visitor clicks it. No data is sent from your server, and neither tag is active unless you add it to a page.
Terms of service: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Zoom — used to automatically create, update, and delete Zoom meetings for virtual class and appointment sessions, only after you connect your own Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app under Settings → Integrations. When a virtual booking is confirmed (and on reschedule or cancellation), your server sends the session’s topic, start time, duration, timezone, and the host’s email address to api.zoom.us / zoom.us using your own credentials. Nothing is sent unless you enable the integration, and visitors’ browsers never contact Zoom through this plugin.
Terms of service: https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://explore.zoom.us/en/privacy/

Postmark — used to send your site’s email through your own Postmark account, only after you connect one under Gather Grove → Settings → Email delivery. When connected, your server sends Postmark your key, your sending domain (to register it and check its DNS records), and each email it is asked to send: sender, recipients, subject, body and any attachments. If you also switch on “Send all your site’s email through Postmark”, every email your site sends goes this way. Postmark then posts delivery, bounce, open, click, spam-complaint and unsubscribe reports back to a secret address on your site. Nothing is sent unless you connect an account.
Terms of service: https://postmarkapp.com/terms-of-service — Privacy policy: https://postmarkapp.com/privacy-policy

Web push services (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft) — when a member turns on phone notifications, their browser registers with its own push service, and your site sends each notification to that service for delivery. The notification carries a short title and a link. The push service receives it with the member’s browser subscription address, and with your site’s admin email address, which the web push standard requires as a contact for the sending site. Nothing is sent unless a member turns notifications on.
Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy — Mozilla privacy policy: https://www.mozilla.org/privacy/ — Apple privacy policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/ — Microsoft privacy statement: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
